query: What drives customer satisfaction (Overall Rating) across the different airlines?

per_column.name: crew_attitude
per_column.rationale: Crew attitude is a plausible major driver of satisfaction and gives a genuine grouping axis. Values are well-grounded in the samples (positive greeting -> positive; no service seen -> negative). The 'positive' label on the deficient-reservation row is defensible since the review calls employees friendly, though it slightly mixes crew vs. non-flight service. Balanced distribution supports discriminative value.

per_column.name: crew_proactivity
per_column.rationale: Distinct from attitude, capturing whether crew anticipated needs; a useful additional axis for modeling service drivers. Samples are well-supported (2.5 hours no service -> absent_neglectful; hard-working crew -> proactive). Reasonable Unknown for silent row.

per_column.name: service_consistency
per_column.rationale: Consistency of service is a reasonable analytical lens with a well-spread distribution. However groundedness is weaker: the itinerary-change row (SQ101 not operating) has no in-flight service description yet was labeled 'consistently_poor', which the text does not support. Some labels appear to conflate overall sentiment with service consistency.

per_column.name: operational_disruption_type
per_column.rationale: A clear, non-trivial categorical axis (delay/cancellation/etc.) directly relevant to satisfaction drivers. Samples are well-read: rescheduling -> flight_delay, non-operating flight -> cancellation. Mostly no_disruption is realistic. Minor ambiguity between delay/cancellation labeling but generally sound.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: Handling quality conditioned on a disruption is a strong driver dimension distinct from disruption type. Values track the text (passive_poor for the rescheduling+bad seat reallocation). Reasonable no_disruption pass-through for calm rows.

per_column.name: post_flight_resolution_quality
per_column.rationale: Captures resolution of complaints, a genuine axis though it overlaps partly with disruption_handling. Grounded reasonably: reservation issue never resolved -> refused_or_ignored; smooth flights -> no_issue_raised. Values are sound readings of the samples.

per_column.name: special_needs_accommodation
per_column.rationale: Heavily skewed (863 false / 37 true), so near-constant and offers limited analytical leverage for the general satisfaction question. Where present the false values are correctly grounded (no mention -> false), so groundedness is fine, but usefulness is weak due to sparsity.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide several genuine, distinct axes (crew attitude, proactivity, disruption type and handling, post-flight resolution) that are highly relevant to modeling satisfaction drivers and are largely well-grounded in the review text. Weaknesses: special_needs_accommodation is near-constant and adds little leverage, and service_consistency shows some grounding drift (labeling rows 'consistently_poor' where the source text lacks in-flight service evidence). Overall the set is analytically useful and mostly faithful to the source.
